This is not something that atko or any administrator would need to manage if they didn't want to, and it is something that any person could take responsibility for - though ideally it would be a collaborative project with perhaps one or a handful of primary editors/leads.

The idea is to document major events - like this recent influx of users from reddit and the subsequent server issues and upgrades - or feature changes, major disputes/discussions in the community (like our kerfuffle over /v/beatingwomen a while back), etc. as well as a periodic cultural temperature measurement poll to see how users feel about Voat. Anything which might be useful for new people interested in Voat's history or culture to learn about.

This would not document things in a play-by-play manner like /r/subredditdrama or /r/circlebroke etc., but rather would be a sort of big picture overview of the community's history and development.

The value would be not only in being a part of our collective heritage and legacy as Voaters, nor just for providing valuable perspective for the site administrators, but for the community in the event that it moves off to a new service or site to retain an awareness of what has gone before - what was good and what was not preferable - to be able to make better decisions.

This sort of project would be suited I think for a method of documentation that individual posts on a subverse cannot adequately fulfil, perhaps a document or set of documents maintained independently of any online service, or maintained on a third party website like a wiki[1] or on github, but collaboration on the project could take place on a subverse created for it.

I had this idea a few minutes ago, and it excites me enough that I would like to take a leading role in it as a project, but I have two other responsibilities already on voat that I would not want to split my attention from presently until they are in a state which requires less time and attention invested. So if this is of interest to anyone reading, I would encourage you to create a subverse to organize from, and let others know about it so that we all may help in collectively contributing to it - especially the oldtimers who have been here since before voat was whoaverse. ;)

[1]: I advise against wikia due to licensing issues and deceptive practices on their part. I would encourage such a project be documented under a permissive license like creative commons or WTFPL.

This decision is not made lightly. Our primary consideration must be the safety of the students, faculty and staff of SDSU. This step is taken to ensure that campus parking facilities and roads are maintained at the high standards our campus community deserves. Maintenance and construction costs have increased dramatically over the last several years. Because we have kept parking rates flat for such a long period, current resources in the SDSU Parking Fund (a self-support operation) are insufficient to meet repair and maintenance needs.   • Parking lot lighting upgrades

Additional information can be found at: http://police.sdsu.edu/dps/images/green_alternatives.pdf
